name: Canvas fingerprint
plain: Draws text and shapes in a hidden canvas and reads back the pixels.
meaning: Tiny differences in fonts, antialiasing and GPU drivers make the image almost unique per device and software stack.

limits.headline: Can draw a hidden picture and use tiny pixel differences to tell devices apart
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Draw text and shapes you never see
Check how your screen and fonts turned them into pixels
Turn that into a number that fits few other devices
Match that number again on a later visit
cannot: Know who you are by itself
Get a clean result in Brave, Tor Browser or Firefox strict mode, which add noise or ask first
Ask your permission in most browsers

story.what_it_is: A page draws hidden text and shapes, then reads back the pixels. Small differences identify the device.

marketing.name: Canvas API
marketing.pitch: A way to draw graphics, animation and image effects with JavaScript.

story.for_you: You see nothing, since the drawing is hidden. But your graphics card, fonts and system settings leave a tiny signature that can help a site recognize you again.
story.for_makers: Canvas is made for games and drawing tools. The same feature is used to build an anonymous ID with no cookie. It is cheap, works everywhere and needs no prompt.

use_cases.example: A browser game like Slither.io or Agar.io draws the whole play field on a canvas many times each second.
A drawing app like Excalidraw or Photopea paints your sketch and exports it as an image.
A chart site draws bars and lines on a canvas so thousands of points update smoothly.
An ad tech script draws a sentence in a hidden canvas and hashes it to recognize you without cookies.
A bank's risk engine draws a hidden image at login to check the device has not changed.
A web whiteboard for class draws what the teacher writes and shares it with students live.
A product page uses canvas to build a quick photo preview of a customized mug or shirt.

technical_bounds: Brave and Firefox RFP add noise or prompts
Same hardware gives the same result
